text:
I've been in a really bad downwards spiral for the last year or so. Lot's of partying (I'm a student), going out to eat, just having a snack there and here etc. Low motivation and non-existing willpower. At the same time, I've been thinking about food and my weight every single day, every time I eat. Feeling guilty and ashamed. Some of my clothes doesn't fit, I've felt ugly, fat, the whole range of self-hatred. And it sucks, so I've been trying to change things. 

First, I've started shopping for clothes. Instead of thinking "I'll buy it when I loose weight", I opt for "I can just use a belt, I can alter it, I can sell it later etc.". This makes me feel GOOD. I feel like I look great, and it has enhanced my confidence a lot. 

Second, I've startet skipping breakfast. It seems like I start the day motivated, and then 'gives up' in the evening. When I'm tired and the days are long. So I figured out, how about skipping breakfast (saving 250kcals ish there), and eat my usual lunch at 11? It's in the morning I have zero cravings and are ready for the day afterall.  I live with my bf and another person so we always eat dinner together. I'm not making the dinner usually, so I have little control over what goes in it. My bf is very aware of the use of oils etc., so he's helping the best he can. I start the day by achieving a goal, and that feels great. I don't overthink the whole dinner-ordeal, and that stops me from eating my feelings (shame, loss of control etc.). 

Third, I've been trying to not eat very late at night. Because I'm not being eaten by guilt every minute of the day, it's so much easier to not "eat my feelings" during the night. 

Fourth, I've been trying to reach my step goal every day by actually going out for walks. I've found a great round that takes about 45 minutes, gets my pulse up and some nice views of the city. 

Fifth, I've almost completely stopped eating late night junk food when I'm out drinking. I go home and make myself a toast. It's easier to go home and eat when I'm not in the state of "I'm the overweight girl with ugly clothes anyway, so who cares if I eat a bunch of crap".  And no, it's not exactly few calories in toast with cheese and ham, but I can at least track the calories AND I don't feel guilty the day after. Win-win. 

I truly believe skipping breakfast is key here, as everything else just seemed impossible when I was feeling like shit every single day, not giving a fuck, but also giving a lot of fucks at the same time.

Tldr; Buying clothes that fit, change my eating routine and walking more has caused an upwards spiral

Yoru and Asa have been a large and great part of these most recent chapters. A couple of panels of Yoru in this most recent chapter have made me go back and look at some of their more important interactions. I thought I'd share the little that I did with you all.

**Empathy and Sympathy**

I believe that Yoru is slowly becoming sympathetic to Asa. Not a crazy theory or anything, but I think it's important to differentiate between empathy and sympathy. Yoru has always been empathetic to Asa because she literally can feel her emotions. So, why do I think Yoru is becoming sympathetic towards Asa and what's the difference. 

[Asa falls into a painful self hatred and starts explaining that being alone might be better than feeling this way.](https://imgur.com/i7p56yg) How does Yoru respond? [Yoru agrees.](https://imgur.com/QulrWB7) OK, so what? Well, what would Yoru agreeing with Asa mean for her plans? It would mean her plans to create a powerful weapon would have to take a backseat to Asa's wellbeing. Yoru is actually considering Asa's feelings in the panels rather than just [using the emotions they share](https://imgur.com/5jipClT) to decide her actions. 

Initially we see that Yoru immediately has to treat Asa differently than planned because she [doesn't fear death as much as her anxiety.](https://imgur.com/ejCzVV9) Where I think we begin to see the [sympathetic side of Yoru emerge is after Asa is stood up.](https://imgur.com/TfVysHp) She could've said "You've been stood up", but she shoulders the burden of Asa's feelings as her own. This is more inline with actually sympathizing with someone instead of merely understanding the feelings they have(I've been there before, etc.)

Finally, when [Asa starts tearing into herself Yoru tries to balance her sadness with a soft reasurance.](https://imgur.com/u5zpHe8) Why did she feel the need to do this? Before this she would usually just disregard Asa's feelings, but she's choosing to engage with them. Then their conversation gets cut short and Yoru says ["Asa stay back!".](https://imgur.com/WHmO8wb) Yoru has begun to care for Asa. Perhaps she is reminded of herself maybe she just pities her, but it's now hard to deny the truth. 

**Going Forward**

I'm a little worried for Asa because Yoru is still a devil and at some point Yoru might not want to come to terms with her feelings of sympathy and instead choose to follow through on her [threat.](https://imgur.com/O5wufk3) Only time will tell.  

Thanks for listening

If you have a novice dog, it can be very helpful to get out places in trial-like environments.

I think a lot of folks think that if they go to a run thru (of any kind - agility, obedience, rally), they have to do the course that has been set up.

Just wanted to tell anyone who doesn't know, that you *don't need to feel any pressure do that*.

Tell them when you sign up that you won't be doing the course, that you're there for experience in the ring and will be doing other things.

Watch some dogs go before you and time how long the average person is taking on the ring. Then when you're about to go in, remind the ring crew/judge you're just there to use your ring time to train, and won't be running the course.

You can even ask the mock judge to be in the ring so you can practice with that distraction, but you can also request they stay out of the ring because your dog isn't ready for that.

Set a timer and work with your dog for however long others have taken in the ring (it was 3 minutes the other day when I went to a rally run thru).

I've been to... god, idk, at *least* a few dozen run thrus with my dogs and no one has ever had an issue with my approach.

[Here's a sped up video of the randomness I did with my young dog at a run thru last weekend](https://imgur.com/a/00E4XP9). It was a great experience for him even though I think we did a grand total of two signs. 🙂
